class.name: World
class.brief_description: The world: the main loop, the level that is running and everything in it.
class.description: Set [code]application/run/main_loop_type[/code] to [code]World[/code] to turn the framework on. It owns what belongs to a level - the game mode, the game state and the list of controllers - while the [GameInstance] it holds owns what outlives one, which is the local players. It is also where the session lives: [method host_game], [method create_dedicated_server] and [method join_game] decide the [enum NetMode], and [method server_travel] moves the server and every client to a new level together. [method has_authority] is true in a game with no peer at all, which is what makes a rule written for a server also correct offline. The nodes it builds sit at fixed paths - [code]/root/NetDriver[/code], [code]/root/GameState[/code], [code]/root/Players[/code] and [code]/root/Pawns[/code] - because that is the address every peer refers to them by.

method.name: create_dedicated_server
method.description: Hosts without a player of its own: no local player, no input routing and no camera work. Becomes a [constant NET_MODE_DEDICATED_SERVER].

method.name: create_default_local_player
method.description: Adds the first human, holding [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_ALL] - every device. This is what a single-player game gets without asking.

method.name: create_local_player
method.description: Adds a human at this machine holding one device. [param device_slot] is a [enum PlayerInput.DeviceSlot] value. A convenience wrapper over the [GameInstance], so scripts have one obvious place to reach local players from.

method.name: disconnect_from_network
method.description: Leaves the session and returns to [constant NET_MODE_STANDALONE].

method.name: find_level
method.description: Searches the tree for the [Level] and adopts it. The framework calls this as a level comes up; [method get_level] is what a project reads.

method.name: find_player_controller_by_player_id
method.description: The controller with the server-assigned [param player_id], or null.

method.name: get_controllers
method.description: Every controller in the world, players and bots alike.

method.name: get_first_player_controller
method.description: Player one. [b]The world owns the player list, so this is where [i]who is player one[/i] is answered[/b] - the game mode does not exist on a client to answer it.

method.name: get_game_instance
method.description: The application-lifetime object built from [code]application/game_framework/game_instance_script[/code]. It lives outside the scene tree and survives a level change.

method.name: get_game_mode
method.description: The rules of the current level. [b]Null on a client[/b] - the rules are the server's, and asking for them there is a mistake worth seeing rather than a silent empty object. Use [method get_game_state] for anything a client has to read.

method.name: get_game_mode_defaults
method.description: The default scenes the game mode declares, readable on [i]every[/i] peer. On a server this is the game mode itself; on a client it is an instance deliberately never added to the tree, because both sides have to agree on what a player is built from even though only one side runs the rules.

method.name: get_game_state
method.description: What every peer is allowed to know about the match, including the player list. Unlike the game mode, this exists on clients too.

method.name: get_input_router
method.description: The node that hands each raw input event to whichever local player owns the device it came from. Built once and never freed with a level.

method.name: get_level
method.description: The level currently running.

method.name: get_local_peer_id
method.description: This peer's id. [constant SERVER_PEER_ID] on a server, and in a game with no peer.

method.name: get_local_player
method.description: The human at [param index] - 0 is player one.

method.name: get_local_player_count
method.description: How many humans are at this machine.

method.name: get_local_role_for
method.description: What this peer may do with [param node]. [b]Authority is not ownership[/b] - the server has authority over every pawn, including one a client owns.

method.name: get_net_driver
method.description: Connections, travel, and the mirroring of everything the server creates. It sits at [code]/root/NetDriver[/code] on every peer, because that is the address remote calls are sent to.

method.name: get_net_mode
method.description: How this process takes part in the session, decided entirely by which of [method host_game], [method create_dedicated_server] and [method join_game] was called.

method.name: get_net_owner_peer
method.description: Which connection [param node] answers to, found by walking up the ownership chain: a pawn is owned by its controller, and a player controller by the peer it was created for. A remote call arriving from any other peer is dropped.

method.name: get_pawn_container
method.description: The fixed parent of every spawned pawn, at [code]/root/Pawns[/code], for the same reason as [method get_players_container].

method.name: get_player_controller_at
method.description: The player controller at [param index], or null.

method.name: get_player_controller_count
method.description: How many player controllers this peer holds.

method.name: get_player_controllers
method.description: Every player controller. On a server that is all of them; on a client it is only its own.

method.name: get_players_container
method.description: The fixed parent of every [PlayerController], at [code]/root/Players[/code]. Controllers hang off it rather than off the level so their node path is the same on every peer no matter what the level scene is called.

method.name: get_remote_role_for
method.description: The other side's view of [param node] - the mirror image of [method get_local_role_for].

method.name: has_authority
method.description: True in every mode but client - [b]including with no peer at all[/b], which is what makes a rule written for a server also correct in a game that never touches the network. Write [code]if not has_authority(): return[/code] and the single-player build takes the same path.

method.name: host_game
method.description: Hosts on this machine and keeps playing on it, becoming a [constant NET_MODE_LISTEN_SERVER].

method.name: is_client
method.description: Whether this process connected to somebody else's server.

method.name: is_dedicated_server
method.description: Whether this is a server with no player of its own.

method.name: is_listen_server
method.description: Whether this is a server somebody is playing on.

method.name: is_networked
method.description: Whether there is a peer at all.

method.name: join_game
method.description: Connects to a server, becoming a [constant NET_MODE_CLIENT]. The level to load arrives from the server, so nothing changes locally until it does.

method.name: load_level
method.description: Tears the current level down and builds [param resource_path] here only, with no travel. The travel paths use it once they have agreed on what to load.

method.name: open_level
method.description: Changes level. On a server this forwards to [method server_travel]; a client cannot change level on its own and is told so.

method.name: register_controller
method.description: Adds a controller to the world's lists. [Controller] does this from [code]_enter_tree[/code], which also catches controllers a designer placed in a level by hand. Idempotent. [b]A subclass overriding [code]_enter_tree[/code] must call the base implementation[/b], or its controller silently never appears in any list.

method.name: server_travel
method.description: Loads [param resource_path] on the server and takes every connected client along: each is told to load, reports back, and is only then handed the world as it stands and logged in. [b]That is why a late join and a level change are the same case[/b], and why nothing is ever sent to a peer that could not receive it.

method.name: unregister_controller
method.description: Takes a controller out again, from [code]_exit_tree[/code] - which always runs before the node is deleted, so the lists can never hold a freed controller.

signal.name: connected_to_server
signal.description: This client reached the server. The level to load follows.

signal.name: connection_failed
signal.description: This client could not reach the server.

signal.name: level_loaded
signal.description: A level finished building, on this peer.

signal.name: net_mode_changed
signal.description: The session role changed - hosting started, a connection was made or lost.

signal.name: peer_connected
signal.description: A peer connected. Server side; it is not yet ready to receive the world.

constants.constant: No peer at all. [method has_authority] is still true, so server rules run unchanged.
A server with no player of its own.
A server somebody is playing on.
Connected to somebody else's server. The only mode where [method has_authority] is false.
No role - the node takes no part in replication.
Somebody else's copy, which only receives updates.
The copy belonging to the human driving it, which may send input for it.
The copy that decides. Everything on the server, and everything in a standalone game.
The peer id a server always has, and the id a game with no peer reports.
